detailed_notes.full_notes: A percentage expresses a part per hundred. Converting any fraction to a percentage involves setting up an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 or multiplying the fraction directly by 100.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Fractions vs Percentages
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A fraction is a part of a unit, whereas a percentage is a part per 100. Multiplying a fraction by 100 converts it directly to a percentage.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Complex percentages can be computed mentally by decomposing them into standard benchmark percentages (50%, 25%, 10%, 5%, 1%). Pre-computation estimation builds number sense and catches operational mistakes.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Algebraic Symmetry of Percentages
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Is x% of y equal to y% of x? Using algebra: (x/100)*y = (x*y)/100 = (y/100)*x = y% of x. Thus, x% of y always equals y% of x.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Values greater than 100% represent quantities that exceed the baseline reference value, acting as scaling multiples or growth factors.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Growth and Scaling
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A growth of 150% means the final amount is 250% (100% base + 150% increase) of the initial quantity.

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 1.4 Practical Applications: KYC (Know Your Contents) & Commerce
detailed_notes.full_notes: Analyzing food packaging labels requires converting proportional weight shares into standardized percentages to compare nutritional value accurately across products of different total weights.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Comparing Proportions
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Always compare ingredient proportions on a per-100g basis rather than comparing total weights directly.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Determine which brand of drink mix contains a higher percentage of badam (almond) powder.
materials_or_prerequisites: Two food mix packages with ingredient weights listed
procedure_or_steps: Record badam powder weight and total product weight for Mix A.
Calculate percentage of badam in Mix A: (badam_weight / total_weight) * 100.
Repeat steps 1 and 2 for Mix B.
Compare the two percentage values to identify the richer mixture.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Mix A: 12g out of 150g = 8%. Mix B: 40g out of 400g = 10%.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: Mix B has a higher proportion of badam powder (10% > 8%).

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 2.1 Doubling a Square and the Diagonal
detailed_notes.full_notes: Constructing a square on the diagonal of an existing square yields an area exactly double the original square's area.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Baudhāyana Śulba-Sūtra
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: The cord stretched across the diagonal of a square produces an area double the size of the original square.

detailed_notes.full_notes: The diagonal of a unit square is sqrt(2), a value bounded between 1.414 and 1.415 with a non-terminating, non-repeating decimal expansion.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Irrationality Intuition
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: sqrt(2) cannot be represented as an exact finite decimal or integer fraction.

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 2.3 Combining Two Squares of Different Sizes
detailed_notes.full_notes: Combining two squares of side lengths 'a' and 'b' creates a new square of side length 'c', where 'c' is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs 'a' and 'b'.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Baudhāyana-Pythagoras Theorem
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: In a right-angled triangle, the area of the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the areas of the squares on the other two sides: a^2 + b^2 = c^2.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Integer sets (a, b, c) satisfying a^2 + b^2 = c^2 are called Baudhāyana triples. Scaling a primitive triple by integer factor k produces scaled triples (ka, kb, kc).

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Prove geometrically that a^2 + b^2 = c^2 using four identical right-angled triangles.
procedure_or_steps: Cut four congruent right-angled triangles with legs a and b, and hypotenuse c.
Arrange them inside a square of side (a + b).
Observe that the unshaded central region forms a tilted square of side c and area c^2.
Rearrange the four triangles into two rectangles of dimensions a x b within the same outer square.
Observe that the remaining unshaded area forms two separate squares of areas a^2 and b^2.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Total outer area (a+b)^2 remains constant; unshaded area c^2 equals unshaded area a^2 + b^2.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: The area c^2 is equal to a^2 + b^2.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Extending two-term ratios to multi-term ratios allows dividing a given total quantity into multiple proportional parts by summing proportional shares.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Partitioning Total Quantity
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: To divide Q in ratio a:b:c, total parts = a+b+c. Shares are (a/total)*Q, (b/total)*Q, and (c/total)*Q.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Representative Fraction is the unitless ratio of distance on a map to actual distance on the ground.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: RF Formula
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: RF = Map Distance / Ground Distance (measured in identical units).

detailed_notes.full_notes: Pie charts display proportional categorical data as circular sectors where sector angle is proportional to category frequency relative to 360 degrees.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Sector Angle Calculation
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Central Angle = (Category Value / Total Value) * 360 degrees.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Two variables x and y are in inverse proportion when an increase in x produces a proportional decrease in y such that x * y = k (constant).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Direct vs Inverse Proportion
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Direct: x/y = constant. Inverse: x * y = constant.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Construct an accurate pie chart from assessment grade data.
materials_or_prerequisites: Compass, protractor, ruler, data table (40 students total: A=12, B=10, C=8, D=6, E=4)
procedure_or_steps: Sum total student count (N = 40).
Calculate central angle for each grade: Angle = (Count / 40) * 360°.
Draw a circle with a compass, draw a radius line, and measure consecutive sector angles using a protractor.
Label each sector with its grade and shade accordingly.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: Pie charts visualize proportional partitions accurately when central angles sum to 360°.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Fractals exhibit self-similarity where small parts resemble the whole shape, seen naturally in ferns, trees, and coastlines.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Self-Similarity
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: A geometric property where an object is exactly or approximately similar to a part of itself.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Mathematical fractals are formed by infinite iterative shape replacement rules. At step n, remaining area, square/triangle counts, and hole numbers follow exponential sequence formulas.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Sierpinski Carpet Sequence
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Remaining squares Rn = 8^n; remaining area An = (8/9)^n.

detailed_notes.full_notes: 3D solids (cuboids, tetrahedrons, prisms) can be unfolded into 2D planar nets. Unfolding nets allows finding the shortest distance between points on a solid surface via straight line segments.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Surface Shortest Path
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: The shortest path between two points on a 3D surface corresponds to a straight line segment on its unfolded 2D net.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Construct the first two steps of the Sierpinski Triangle fractal on paper.
procedure_or_steps: Draw an initial solid equilateral triangle (Step 0).
Mark the midpoints of all 3 sides and join them to form 4 smaller identical equilateral triangles.
Remove/shade out the central inverted triangle (Step 1; 3 upright triangles remain).
Repeat the midpoint construction and central removal on each of the 3 remaining upright triangles (Step 2; 9 smaller triangles remain).
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Step 0: 1 triangle; Step 1: 3 triangles, 1 hole; Step 2: 9 triangles, 4 holes.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: At step n, the number of remaining triangles is 3^n.

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 5.1 The Mean as a Visual Fulcrum Point
detailed_notes.full_notes: Placing data points as dots on a horizontal number line reveals the arithmetic mean as the unique balance point (fulcrum) where sum of left distances equals sum of right distances.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Balance Condition
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Sum of (Mean - x_i) for x_i < Mean equals Sum of (x_j - Mean) for x_j > Mean.

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 5.2 Effects of Adding, Removing, or Shifting Data
detailed_notes.full_notes: Adding a data point above the mean shifts the mean upward; adding a point below shifts it downward; adding a point equal to the mean leaves it unchanged.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Uniform Transformations
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Adding constant k to every data point increases the mean by k. Multiplying every point by k scales the mean by k.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Line graphs connect discrete data coordinates sequentially to reveal trend directions, rate of change slopes, and temporal patterns.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Choosing Axis Scales
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Uniform axis spacing is essential to accurately represent rates of change without visual distortion.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Demonstrate physically that the arithmetic mean balances distance moments on a beam.
materials_or_prerequisites: Meter stick, uniform weight washers, fulcrum pivot wedge
procedure_or_steps: Place washers at positions 20 cm, 30 cm, and 70 cm on the meter stick.
Calculate mean position: (20 + 30 + 70) / 3 = 120 / 3 = 40 cm.
Place the pivot wedge exactly at 40 cm.
Observe whether the meter stick balances horizontally.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Left distances = (40-20) + (40-30) = 20 + 10 = 30 cm. Right distance = (70-40) = 30 cm. Beam balances perfectly.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: The arithmetic mean corresponds precisely to the physical center of mass / fulcrum.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Representing an unknown starting number with a variable 'x' proves why performing a specific sequence of operations always yields a predictable constant result regardless of the initial choice.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Number Trick Mechanics
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Think of x -> Add 5 (x+5) -> Multiply by 2 (2x+10) -> Subtract 10 (2x) -> Divide by 2 (x). Returns starting number x.

detailed_notes.full_notes: In number pyramids, each upper cell is the sum of two lower adjacent cells. Modeling bottom row cells with variables sets up linear equations to solve missing entries.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Additive Grid Rule
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: If bottom cells are a, b, c, then middle cells are (a+b), (b+c), and top cell is a + 2b + c.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Arranging given digits into two numbers to maximize their product requires making higher place-value digits as large as possible while minimizing the absolute difference between the two numbers.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Max Product Rule
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: For a fixed sum, two numbers produce the maximum product when they are as close to equal as possible.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Create an algebraic step procedure that decodes a secret birth month and day.
procedure_or_steps: Ask peer to take birth month number M (1-12).
Multiply M by 5 (5M).
Multiply result by 4 (20M + 24).
Multiply result by 5 (100M + 165).
Add birth day D (100M + D + 165).
Ask peer for final total T. Subtract 165 from T.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Result T - 165 = 100M + D. Hundreds digits give Month M; remaining two digits give Day D.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: Algebraic expansion guarantees complete recovery of two secret variables.

detailed_notes.section_number_and_title: 7.1 Area of Rectangles, Squares, and Parallelograms
detailed_notes.full_notes: Area measures the 2D surface enclosed inside a boundary. Transforming a parallelogram into an equivalent rectangle of identical base and height shows Area = Base * Height.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Parallelogram to Rectangle
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Cutting a right triangle off one side of a parallelogram and translating it to the opposite side forms a rectangle with Area = base * height.

detailed_notes.full_notes: Any triangle is exactly half of a parallelogram with the same base and height (Area = 1/2 * b * h). A trapezium splits into two triangles or a rectangle and triangles, yielding Area = 1/2 * (a + b) * h.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Trapezium Area
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Area of trapezium = 0.5 * (Sum of parallel sides) * (Perpendicular distance between them).

detailed_notes.full_notes: Shapes with identical perimeters can enclose drastically different surface areas, and shapes with identical areas can have vastly different perimeters.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Area vs Perimeter
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Perimeter is 1D boundary length; Area is 2D enclosed surface size. One does not dictate the other.

stem_lab_drawers.aim_or_objective: Determine the exact area of an irregular polygon drawn on a square grid.
materials_or_prerequisites: 1 cm dot grid paper, ruler, pencil
procedure_or_steps: Draw polygon on 1 cm grid paper.
Count full unit grid squares completely enclosed inside shape.
Count half unit grid squares (take every two half squares as 1 full sq cm).
Decompose remaining triangular or trapezoidal regions into standard base-height formulas.
Sum partial areas to compute total surface area.
stem_lab_drawers.observations_or_results: Combining grid counts and sub-shape dissection gives precise square centimeter total.
stem_lab_drawers.conclusion_or_principle: Irregular polygon areas equal the sum of their non-overlapping component sub-areas.
